records.our_prose: St. George's low-elevation Dixie belt (Mojave-edge high desert) runs cucumbers on one spring cycle only, per USU Extension's Suggested Vegetable Planting Dates for Utah. Direct-sow around March 15, the Group C (Tender) date for St. George, about two weeks ahead of the March 30 average last frost; the table's explicit local date runs earlier than a generic frost-relative rule would. Harvest begins about 58 days later, around May 12, and continues into late June. Once St. George's daytime highs push past 95°F and the county's own frost-and-elevation data show summer highs routinely reaching 100°F in June through August, vines stop setting fruit and any that does form turns bitter. USU documents fall planting for cool-season crops in the St. George area but gives no fall or summer-replant window for cucumbers, so there is no second cycle here; frost returns around November 1, well after the plants have already stopped producing for the year.

records.our_prose: In the warm arid Southwest (southern New Mexico and West Texas, zone 8), cucumber is a warm-season crop with a long window. Sow after the last frost once the soil warms, with successions into early summer; the intense heat and low humidity make steady, deep watering and mulch essential to prevent bitterness and spider mites. A fall sowing extends harvest into the mild autumn.
